rationale: C09 is a near-verbatim, single-sentence precedent for the child: both authorize a specifically named woman to be appointed to a competitive civil-service position while waiving the competitive provisions of the governing civil-service rules. The child chiefly adapts the person's name and slightly modernizes or broadens the position and waiver wording. C22 uses the same machinery and sentence structure but concerns a named man and a specified department; C16 is also closely parallel but uses less exact language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Mrs. Beth Campbell Short may be appointed to a permanent competitive position in the classified civil service of the United States without regard to the competitive provisions of the Civil Service Rules and Regulations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Mrs. Cressie E. Coffelt may be appointed to a competitive position in the Department of the Interior without compliance with the competitive provisions of the Civil Service Act and Rules.
shared_material.explanation: The provisions share the complete operative template: named individual, authorization to appoint, competitive position, and express waiver of competitive civil-service requirements.
The identical opening introduces the closely matched operative sentence; although conventional alone, it reinforces the extensive substantive correspondence.
